To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AdS/CFT correspondence can be used to study quantum systems in condensed-matter physics and that the AdS(5) x S(5) string sigma-model is an example of an integrable quantum system.
We propose a method to compute the energy level spacing of the AdS_5xS^5 superstring based on the integrability of the model and the underlying algebraic curve.

(i) the string energy levels are determined from the eigenvalues of a matrix of size 8x8; (ii) the matrix has a simple form and can be easily evaluated numerically for any classical string configuration, and (iii) the eigenvalues can be labeled with the help of a set of 8 conserved charges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantum mechanics of the superstring in AdS(4)xCP(3) and AdS(5) xS(5).

the quantum spectrum of string theory on the AdS(5) x S(5) background, which is the near-horizon geometry of the D3-branes in the type IIB superstring theory and the background of the AdS/CFT correspondence.
the study of the AdS/CFT correspondence in the regime of strong coupling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the agreement of the results obtained by the algebraic curve method with the results obtained by other methods is very good and that the algebraic curve provides a powerful and systematic tool to study the quantum spectrum of the string in AdS(2)xS(4).
our results for the SU(3) case are in agreement with those of the literature and that the SU(2), SL(2) and BMPP results are in disagreement.

the results of the present paper, together with the results of [1], [2] and [3], provide a complete and consistent description of the quantum spectrum of the AdS(5) x S(5) superstrings, in the limit of the classical string solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectrum of the string in AdS(3)xS(3) can be computed by using the algebraic curve associated to the string sigma model.
we have developed an algorithm to compute the spectrum of any string solution in AdS(2)xS(2).
we provide an unambiguous prescription to label the quantum states of the superstring in AdS(4)xCP(3) or in AdS(3)xS(2) x S(1) in terms of the classical string configuration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequencies of the fluctuations are given in terms of the zeros of a single analytic function, the so called "spectral curve".
the spectrum of excitations around classical string solutions can be extracted from the algebraic curves of the corresponding classical solutions.
the spectrum is not given by a simple harmonic oscillator, and that the frequencies are not all integers.
